artists.biography: Haken (/ˈheɪkən/) are an English progressive metal band formed in 2007 by multi-instrumentalist Richard Henshall, guitarist Matthew Marshall, and vocalist Ross Jennings. While Henshall, Marshall, and Jennings first had the idea of forming Haken in 2004, they opted to pursue their instruments and songwriting first. Upon recruiting other members three years later, they eventually released the demo Enter the 5th Dimension in 2008, signing with Sensory Records and releasing their first album Aquarius in 2010. As of 2020, they have released six studio albums, an EP, and two live albums.

perplexity.description:
Fauna," released on March 3, 2023, is the seventh studio album by British progressive rock band Haken, issued through Inside Out Music and Sony Music. The album marks the return of keyboardist Peter Jones as a full member, contributing significantly to its diverse sonic palette. Musically, "Fauna" blends progressive metal and rock with a broad stylistic range, from djent-inspired rhythms to melodic and jazz-influenced passages. Conceptually, each track is themed around an animal, linking natural and human elements in layered, intricate compositions that showcase the band's evolving sound and compositional ambition.

Within Haken's discography, "Fauna" stands out as their most genre-busting and conceptually ambitious work to date, reflecting an "anything goes" approach that expands their progressive canon while maintaining accessibility. The album features complex arrangements and emotional depth, highlighted in tracks like the 11-minute "Elephants Never Forget" and the poignant closing song "Eyes of Ebony," which connects to personal themes of loss. Critically, "Fauna" received positive reviews for its musicianship, songwriting, and production quality, earning high marks from progressive music critics and resonating well with the band's fanbase. Commercially, it achieved moderate success within the progressive metal scene.
